title: Behavioral anchor for the NT-sign convention: sugar/bitter feeding
prediction_source: Shiu et al. 2024 Fig 3a (bitter GRN co-stimulation suppresses sugar-driven MN9_L firing)

substrate.snapshot: run-007: male-cns:v0.9 depth-2 closed subgraph around the 36 driven GRNs (40,290 neurons, 336,245 signed edges, 0 dangling)
substrate.driven_sugar: LB3b/LB3c (Gr64f+ sugar lbGRNs), right hemisphere, n=17
substrate.driven_bitter: LB1a-d (Gr33a+ bitter lbGRNs), right hemisphere, n=19
substrate.population_mapping_source: Agee et al. 2026 (Cell) gustatory connectome paper: MaleCNS-native lbGRN type names; mapping recorded in wp6c_grn_seeds.json with per-neuron NT
substrate.readout: MN9_L (10331) firing rate - the paper's readout (id_mn9 720575940660219265, left; right-GRN drive -> left MN9, contralateral crossing). MN9_R (16949) recorded, not headline.

protocol.drive: sugar 200 Hz, bitter 200 Hz - the paper's Fig 3a high-drive corner (its full grid is 0-200 Hz in 20 Hz steps)
protocol.simulator: fly.dynamics.lif.simulate_lif (WP6b-validated against Shiu Brian2 reference, TOST p~0, rho=0.9999)
protocol.two_population_drive: stimulated2/r_poisson2_Hz pathway (reference poi() exc2 semantics; rfc=0; TDD'd in tests/test_two_population_drive.py)

arms.signed: pipeline NT convention: gaba, glutamate -> -1; ach -> +1; unknown -> +1 (5,794/40,290 neurons unknown, hub-under-represented)
arms.abl-glu: glutamate -> +1 (gaba kept inhibitory): 32,165 glutamatergic edges flipped positive
arms.all-pos: all weights positive (sign convention fully removed)

discriminating_outcome.verdict: PASS - the signed convention reproduces the paper's directional finding (bitter suppresses sugar-driven MN9_L firing) and BOTH ablated conventions fail to reproduce it. The NT-sign assumption is load-bearing: GABA alone is insufficient - glutamatergic inhibition is specifically required for bitter-driven feeding suppression.
discriminating_outcome.exact_zero_note: MN9_L suppression is literal zero spikes in 10/10 signed trials (not a rounding artifact). The paper's own pipeline represents MN9 rates as fillna(0) and its Fig 3a shows full suppression at high bitter drive - complete silencing at the 200/200 corner matches the published target regime.

interpretation.signed: Bitter co-drive silences MN9_L (81.3 -> 0.0 Hz; Welch t=101.2, p=4.6e-15; Mann-Whitney p=6.1e-05), reproducing the paper's Fig 3a direction on MaleCNS.
interpretation.abl-glu: With glutamate excitatory, bitter co-drive INCREASES MN9_L rate (102.7 -> 105.7 Hz; Welch p=1.6e-04): suppression depends on glutamatergic inhibition, not only GABA. Corroborates Agee et al. 2026: lbGRN bitter signaling is (partly) glutamatergic.
interpretation.all-pos: Without signs, MN9_L runs at ~143 Hz in both conditions (no suppression; delta +0.5 Hz, Welch p=0.031 - a small but significant INCREASE), plus a 16x spike-count explosion (618K vs 39K mean): the unsigned graph is not merely quantitatively wrong, it produces a qualitatively different (epileptiform) network.

limitations: Population identity mapping (FlyWire GRNs -> MaleCNS lbGRN types) is from the Agee et al. 2026 (Cell) gustatory connectome paper, not from Shiu et al.; literature-based, recorded in wp6c_grn_seeds.json with per-neuron NT.
Directionality, not rate matching, is the tested prediction (different substrate: MaleCNS vs the paper's FlyWire male-CNS model).
MN9 firing rate is a scalar circuit proxy for proboscis extension, not a behavioral assay.
NT convention for 'unknown' neurons (14.4% here) defaults to +1; hub-bias check (WP6b) shows unknown-NT neurons are under-represented among out-weight hubs.
Single grid corner (200/200 Hz) tested, not the paper's full 11x11 grid; a dose-response reproduction would be the natural follow-up.
MN9_R (16949) is silent across all arms/conditions in this closure (dynamics of the right-side mirror circuit may require the left GRNs); the paper's readout (MN9_L) is the one reported.
